def: Finding vectors that are probably among the closest to a query while comparing only a small fraction of the collection.
The fraction of the exact top-k neighbours that an approximate index returns, measured against brute-force search over the same vectors.
Comparing the query with every stored vector, which is exact but costs one similarity per vector.
A vector index that clusters vectors with k-means and, at query time, scans only the few cells whose centroids are nearest the query.
The number of IVF cells scanned per query, which trades recall against the number of distance computations.
Compressing a vector by cutting it into sub-vectors and storing, for each, the one-byte id of its nearest centroid in a learned codebook.
Scoring an uncompressed query against compressed vectors by summing lookups in per-sub-vector distance tables.
Hierarchical Navigable Small World graph: a layered proximity graph searched greedily from sparse upper layers down to a dense bottom layer.
The width of the candidate list used when searching an HNSW graph, raised to gain recall at the cost of latency.
The number of links each HNSW node keeps, which raises achievable recall and memory use together.
A graph that links each vector to some of its near neighbours so a search can walk towards a query.
Storing each number of a vector in fewer bits, such as 8, to cut memory at a small cost in accuracy.
